Hi Ranjeet,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX! Yes, CODEX is downloaded in R and thus as long as you have R in your LINUX system you can use it! The input needs to include the exonic target file, aka, the bed file, in addition to the bam files. Also needed is a vector of sample names.

Cheers,
Yuchao


On Jan 31, 2016, at 1:15 AM, Ranjeet Thergaonkar <rant...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear Dr Yuchao
I read your paper on CODEX and was really impressed by the fact that robust analysis for CNV van be extracted from WES data.
I am a pediatric nephrologist exploring the genetics of a complex disorder, vesicoureteral reflux. I have WES data on cases and controls using capture by Agilent SureSelect v2 exome (RNA baits). I wish to look for CNV's in this data (and need to convinvce my bioinformatician to do the same!). My background knowledge of bioinformaticcs is very sparse and hence I have some very basic questions for you:
1. Is CODEX downloaded into a linux system?
2. What input files are required besides the bam files?

Regards
Ranjeet
